w: Piran's largest and main town square is named for the Baroque violinist and composer Giuseppe Tartini, honoured since 1896 by a bronze monument at its centre. It anchors the old town of this Adriatic port in southwestern Slovenia, the space every lane in the walled centre eventually reaches.
s: Piran's grand square, named for its Baroque-born son
_facts: Largest and main town square in Piran
Named after violinist and composer Giuseppe Tartini

w: St. George's Parish Church stands on the hill above Piran's old town, a Roman Catholic church built in the Venetian Renaissance style. Dedicated to Saint George, it was the life's work of the Venetian stonemason Bonfante Torre, who gave this Adriatic port town its most prominent hilltop landmark.
s: Hilltop church built by a Venetian stonemason
_facts: Roman Catholic church on the hill above Piran
Built in the Venetian Renaissance architectural style
The life's work of stonemason Bonfante Torre of Venice

w: Giuseppe Tartini, the Baroque violinist and composer for whom Piran's main square is named, was born in this house. It stands directly on Tartini Square, marking the spot where the town's most famous musical son first drew breath, a modest domestic counterpoint to the grand plaza outside its door.
s: Where Piran's famous violinist first drew breath
_facts: Birthplace of violinist and composer Giuseppe Tartini
Located on Tartini Square in Piran

w: The Walls of Piran are the town's defensive fortifications, built to protect this coastal settlement on the Adriatic Sea in southwestern Slovenia. Significant portions remain well preserved, making them one of the more intact examples of historic town walls surviving along this stretch of coast.
s: Piran's old sea walls, still standing strong
_facts: Defensive walls of the town of Piran
Significant parts of the fortification remain well preserved

w: The Piran Minorite Monastery is a Roman Catholic monastery dedicated to St. Francis, operated by the Order of Friars Minor Conventual in the port town of Piran on Slovenia's Adriatic coast. It remains an active religious house within Piran's walled historic centre.
s: The Franciscans' quiet corner of old Piran
_facts: Operated by the Order of Friars Minor Conventual

w: Secovlje Salina Landscape Park protects the salt pans near the village of Secovlje, southwest of Piran. Its salt evaporation ponds cover about 16 hectares, while the wider saltworks along the mouth of the Dragonja River extend across some 650 hectares, a landscape park built entirely around the business of making salt.
s: Salt still made the old way outside Piran
_facts: Landscape park covering the Secovlje Saltpans near Piran
Saltworks along the Dragonja River span about 650 hectares

w: Piran Aquarium has operated since 1964 opposite the town's maritime museum, at the inner quay of the port. Visitor numbers once topped 60,000 a year before 1991, later halving; the University of Primorska's science centre now runs it, and a 2022 refit added a children's corner and marine-shade paint.
s: Small aquarium by the quay, running since '64
_facts: Operating since 1964, next to Piran's inner quay
Part of the University of Primorska science centre
Pre-1991 visitor numbers topped 60,000 a year, later halved
